Move the Beam-network upsert/check (1595-1683) and _save_identified merge logic (1480-1593) into a dedicated persistence module. Delete the dead _try_* wrappers (see dead_or_dup).

hotspots.problem: Leadpipe and Capturify parsers are ~90% copy-paste: same IP-equality loop, same _record_matches_visitor call, same weak-confidence capping, same email-from-emails[] fallback. _parse_leadpipe_person and _parse_capturify_person are near-identical with only confidence_score and a couple field aliases differing. hotspots.problem: Heuristic domain synthesis builds a candidate domain by string-munging the IPinfo org name ('Acme Corp' -> 'acmecorp.com') via a chain of .replace() calls and a length heuristic. Fragile and hard to reason about; mis-synthesized domains feed Hunter/Apollo which then return a random employee at a possibly-wrong company. Naming (_org_to_domain) hides that it can fabricate a domain that was never observed.
hotspots.refactor: Restrict synthesis to exact/partial map hits only, or gate every heuristic candidate behind the existing _verify_domain_exists DNS check before returning it (currently DNS-checked later in _call_ipinfo_api, but the heuristic still emits arbitrary strings). Rename to _org_to_domain_or_guess to signal the fabrication risk.

hotspots.problem: Single 170-line function running the entire A-F pipeline: enrichment, OSINT scan, candidate derivation, concurrent Maigret+rule-base, identity verification, paid-fallback budget logic, persistence, and Gemini deep research — with multiple re-computations of confirmed_count and unified after each stage. Hard to test stages in isolation; the paid-fallback branch (231-263) is deeply nested.
hotspots.refactor: Extract stage helpers (gather_free_signals, maybe_run_paid, build_blob) each returning the running account set + counts; have resolve_social compose them. The paid budget/log block is a self-contained unit that belongs in its own coroutine.

hotspots.problem: IP->domain cache read/write is inlined into resolve() with a subtle double-negative guard `if company_domain is None and (not self.redis or not await self._redis_has_key(cache_key))`. hotspots.refactor: Extract a _cached_ip_company(visitor) coroutine returning (domain|None, was_cached) so resolve() reads as `domain, hit = await self._cached_ip_company(...)`.

hotspots.problem: handlePlanClick mixes three concerns (free routing, anon-vs-authed gate via api.getToken(), and Lemon Squeezy checkout) and silently swallows the createCheckout error into a redirect with empty catch. A signed-in user whose checkout call fails gets bounced to /dashboard/billing with no error surfaced — they will see no reason their click 'did nothing'.

hotspots.problem: Public marketing page reads api.getToken() to branch on auth. In the Clerk world the legacy localStorage token is never set, so the only thing populating getToken() here is ClerkTokenSync running in the layout; if that hasn't synced yet on a fresh public-page load the authed user is treated as anonymous and sent to /signup instead of straight to checkout. Coupling a public page to the auth-client singleton is a leaky abstraction.
hotspots.refactor: Use Clerk's useAuth().isSignedIn (already the source of truth elsewhere, e.g. app/page.tsx) to decide signed-in vs anonymous rather than the token cache.

hotspots.problem: Pixel gzips to 5003 bytes (measured: gzip -c src/tracker.js | wc -c = 5003). CLAUDE.md mandates <5KB gzipped; the file is already 3 bytes over 5000 and any further feature pushes it past the documented budget. The file has grown to a god-pixel: fingerprinting (17 signals), engagement scoring, SPA nav interception, form capture, UTM identify, queue persistence, AND third-party vendor stacking all in one IIFE.
hotspots.refactor: Trim to fit budget without losing function: (a) drop the webglFp() extension lookup or the canvasFp() — each fingerprint signal that needs try/catch adds disproportionate bytes; (b) collapse the 4 lsGet/lsSet/lsDel wrappers; (c) gate the identity-vendor stacking block (lines 383-404) behind a separately-loaded chunk since it is strictly opt-in and most installs never use it. Set up a CI check that fails when gzip size >= 5000 so this never silently regresses in prod.

hotspots.problem: Magic fingerprint signal `Math.tan(-1e300)` with no comment. This is a known FP-Collect engine-detection trick (V8 vs SpiderMonkey return different values), but to a maintainer it reads like dead/garbage code and is a prime candidate for accidental deletion.
hotspots.refactor: Add a one-line comment naming the technique and why (JS-engine discriminator), or extract to a named helper `engineTanFp()`. Zero behavior change.

hotspots.problem: Two divergent Python dependency manifests. Root requirements.txt (what the Dockerfile installs, per the comment at line 52-53) is MISSING packages that apps/api/requirements.txt pins: sendgrid, maxminddb, geoip2, pyjwt[crypto], pytest-httpx, pytest. Conversely root has anthropic/celery/apscheduler that overlap. Pins also differ (asyncpg==0.29.0 pinned in root vs >=0.29.0 floor in api). A reader cannot tell which file is authoritative, and CLAUDE.md memory explicitly warns 'All Python deps must be in requirements.txt for CI — don't play whack-a-mole'.
hotspots.refactor: Make root requirements.txt the single source of truth and have apps/api/requirements.txt either be removed or do `-r ../../requirements.txt`. Reconcile the pin mismatches (asyncpg) in one pass. Verify against actual imports before deleting any line — this is prod-deploy-critical.

hotspots.problem: Base image is python:3.11-slim-bookworm, but CLAUDE.md tech stack and pyproject context describe Python 3.12. The 3.11 pin is deliberate (Playwright/Bookworm comment) but undocumented as a stack deviation — a future reader 'fixing' the version to match docs would break the documented Playwright workaround.
hotspots.refactor: Add a single comment line noting the intentional 3.11 (not 3.12) choice and that it is independent of the Bookworm pin, or update CLAUDE.md to state 3.11. No code change.

hotspots.problem: 11 wildcard star-imports (`from apps.api.models.X import *  # noqa: F401,F403`) used purely to register SQLAlchemy mappers for create_all. This leaks every symbol from each module into the seed namespace, defeats linting, and is fragile copy-paste that must be hand-maintained as models are added.
hotspots.refactor: Replace the model star-imports with a single explicit `import apps.api.models  # noqa: F401` if the models package __init__ imports all model modules (common pattern), or list the concrete class names. Removes 11 noqa lines and the namespace pollution.

[site] bucket = "./src" is inert: worker.js never reads from the static-assets KV binding it creates (404s all non-/t.js paths). Deprecated Workers Sites config that does nothing but upload tracker.js to KV on each deploy.

Two overlapping-but-divergent dependency lists. ~20 packages appear in both with some pin differences (asyncpg==0.29.0 vs >=0.29.0), and each file has packages the other lacks (root lacks sendgrid/maxminddb/geoip2/pyjwt/pytest; api lacks resend-only-floor differences, celery, apscheduler, anthropic versions). The Dockerfile installs ONLY root requirements.txt (comment at root line 52-53 explicitly warns about this), so anything in apps/api/requirements.txt but not root is absent from the prod image. Consolidate to one source of truth.
